title.narrative: Activity under preparation Fit for Market Africa 2030 - Direct award à COLEAD

description.narrative: Contract related to: Fit for Market Africa 2030 - Direct award à COLEAD - The Action aims to enable agribusinesses, MSMEs, farmer groups, and farmers to maintain and improve access to domestic, regional and EU market, benefitting from the AfCFTA commitments, EPAs and other preferential trade arrangements with the EU (main focus on fruit and vegetables, but open to other agri-food value chains). The Action will increase the resilience, fairness (inclusiveness), competitiveness and sustainability of a selected number of agricultural value chains, through the development and adoption of safe and sustainable practices, skills and technologies, as well as boosting equal access to finance and investments, which in turn are expected to contribute to decent job creation and the sustainable and inclusive transformation of the agri-food sector in the target countries. Skilled and resilient agri-food operators from both private and public sectors are key in order to promote inclusive, sustainable, low carbon and (climate) resilient agricultural value chains. In this context, the action will focus on two mutually reinforcing components: 1) Continental facility; 2) Country facility.Component 1 (continental facility ¿ Sustainable horticulture in SSA) Important challenges and bottlenecks are impairing the competitiveness of the horticultural sector in Africa. The enabling environment struggles to effectively support the private sector by providing adequate and cost-effective services such as extension, regulation, certification, logistics and in general enabling a predictable and stable business environment.This component seeks to strengthen national horticultural production and distribution systems across SSA countries. This means supporting agri-food MSMEs (including farmer groups and cooperatives), local services providers in the horticultural sector and the national competent authorities, to strengthen their capabilities and support a strong African horticultural sector. By improving access to domestic, regional and international markets for fruit and vegetable value chains, as well as access to finance and investment, this component will create an operational and enabling platform that contributes to the overall transformation of food systems in SSA within a sustainable framework. Component 1 will also seek the development of partnerships with African educational institutions to develop massive open vocational capacity building. Component 2 (Selected country-agrifood value chain facility)The European Union continues to be a highly appealing market for African agricultural goods, while intra-continental exchanges are also gaining importance. Agri-food exports from SSA economies to the EU are of pivotal importance in terms of generating income and employment, and key contributors towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Nonetheless, meeting evolving EU Regulations and Standards remains a major and challenging determinant for market access, as well as competitiveness.
